title: add vpc control plane: advanced peering, endpoints, and route53 dns support
author: Connor Lee
description: Motivation: Private control plane installs need a repeatable Terraform + Helm configuration that supports multi-AZ subnets, VPC peering, interface endpoints, security groups, and Route53 private hosted zone peering. Customers deploying Redwood Private have repeatedly asked for a single opinionated module that wires peering, DNS, and endpoints together and can be consumed by the private installer with sensible defaults. This PR implements an advanced VPC control-plane Terraform module, updates the Helm chart for the control-plane to support external-dns and endpoint-driven discovery, and adds upgrade/rollback guidance for peering and DNS record changes.  What this changes: 1) Terraform: adds terraform/modules/vpc-control-plane with resources for subnets (multi-az), aws_vpc_peering_connection, aws_vpc_endpoint (interface/route53), security groups and route53_zone_association helpers. Module exposes inputs for cidr ranges, allowed CIDRs, peer VPC IDs, tags, and toggle flags for creating endpoints vs using existing ones. 2) Helm: control-plane chart now has values.enableExternalDNS, values.network.peerVpcIds, and a configmap template to inject resolver endpoints for the control-plane components. 3) Installer: private installer (installer/aws) now calls the module and writes out peering status to the control-plane config for automated rollouts. 4) Networking code: adds peering_manager.go with idempotent reconciliation for peering state during upgrade operations. 5) Docs: docs/private/deploy-vpc.md with step-by-step and rollback playbook.  Testing and CI: added unit tests for Terraform module (terraform validate in pipeline), Helm linting and template rendering checks, and a small e2e smoke test in perf-canary that verifies DNS resolution across a peered VPC when using the module. Initial CI run hit a transient provider rate-limit error on aws_vpc_peering_connection; pipeline was retried and passed.  Backward compatibility and migration notes: module defaults to not modify existing Route53 zones unless explicit opt-in values are set. Peering creation is gated behind a new flag create_peering to avoid accidental cross-account peering. Upgrades that enable external DNS will create SRV/A records; we document a rollback path that removes DNS records first and then tears down peering if needed.  Checklist: - [x] Terraform module implementation and tests - [x] Helm chart changes + linting - [x] Installer integration + smoke e2e - [x] Documentation and upgrade/rollback guide - [x] Security review of SG rules (allowed only required ports)  Related: ENG-4123 (tracking module design), ENG-4139 (installer integration), referenced earlier PRs that incrementally added simpler VPC wiring (see pr-71234, pr-74512).  Deploy notes: recommend running terraform plan with the new variables in a staging account. For cross-account peering, ensure accepter side accepts connection externally; module exposes peering tags to make manual acceptance auditable. Monitor control-plane logs for DNS resolution errors for first 30 minutes after peering completes.

review_comments: Priya Patel: Please confirm cross-account peering workflow and add acceptance test for accepter-side behavior. Also request explicit SG egress rules rather than open 0.0.0.0/0 for simplicity.
Connor Lee: Responded - added create_peering flag and documentation for cross-account acceptance; tightened SG egress to control-plane CIDRs only.
Maya Chen: Found an edge case where route53 association fails if zones are owned by different accounts; requested safer defaults (dont_associate_route53 = true).
Connor Lee: Responded - introduced dont_associate_route53 boolean and added clear warnings in docs; updated terraform tests to cover both flows.
Lukas Müller: CI flake on terraform validate (provider rate limit) during first run. Reran pipeline; all checks green. Approved for merge.
release_notes: Add terraform module for VPC control plane provisioning (subnets, peering, endpoints), Helm chart support for external DNS and resolver injection, and installer integration. Includes docs and rollback guidance.
